The primary series supplies three bounded size points under a declared input and precision policy. Orders and identity powers differ across integers, and N15 has especially favorable identity multipliers. Ripple has more logical wires and compiled Boolean work; the declared model favors its lower arbitrary-rotation workload here. QDK reduces the circuit to canonical non-Clifford/measurement counts on placeholder wires, and PSSPC does not preserve the actual Clifford dependency graph. The projected times therefore remain conditional on that abstraction; the study is neither a universal physical scaling fit nor a classical factoring benchmark.

The Gidney–Ekerå construction is a useful external end-to-end reference: it combines optimized arithmetic and recovery with a surface-code layout, magic-state factories, repeated attempts and a specified controller reaction time

. Its RSA-2048 estimate uses 20 million noisy qubits and an expected eight-hour runtime under a particular nearest-neighbor hardware model. Those numbers are not extrapolations from our N15/N21 circuits.

A later Gidney preprint trades more time for less space, using approximate residue arithmetic, dense idle storage and smaller magic-state production. Its headline estimate is below a million noisy qubits and below a week, with the same stated physical error, cycle and controller assumptions as the earlier reference
. The paper’s dense-storage choice uses yoked surface codes, whose published memory results concern a hierarchical code over a nearest-neighbor square grid
. A lower memory cost is not automatically a faster complete algorithm: transfers between storage and computation, factory throughput, arithmetic retries and controller latency still matter.

Checks for the physical scaling study

children.label: Checks for the physical scaling study

children.value: The scaling study derives ideal probabilities from independent FFTs of classical modular-power residue indicators and compares them with the geometric Fourier reference. The actual continued-fraction, modular-period verification and gcd rule defines factor success. The independent order reference is evaluated after circuit materialization and never supplies gate constants or chooses phase precision.

Every distinct ripple power multiplier is checked on all valid input/control branches with clean work restoration. Independent review checks the corresponding Fourier powers on coherent superpositions over the valid domain. Tiny actual full circuits and controlled multipliers are compared with independent classical and complex-amplitude answers. Bounded sparse simulation also rechecks the N15/t8 and N21/t6 ripple circuits. The larger N21/t10 and N35/t12 materializations have arithmetic and resource checks; no fresh full-state simulation or formal proof is claimed for them. Exported QASM, native-input hashes, readout mappings, complete retry counts and model allocations are checked separately.
No Lean formalization is integrated for this generator.
Formalization is available at several layers. Peng and colleagues published an end-to-end ideal Shor development in Coq, including returned-factor correctness and a repeated-trial failure bound

, extraction-oriented circuit correspondence, and logical gate-count results. Coq/Rocq and Lean are different proof assistants. The upstream extraction route explicitly retains assumptions about OCaml floats, Zarith arithmetic, the measurement simulator and handwritten I/O.
A 2026 Lean preprint is a concrete additional reference

exposes separate declared-oracle Shor, measured-arithmetic RSA logical models and fixed RSA-2048 endpoints. The declared-oracle model’s oracle coordinate is not a compiled modular-arithmetic gate count. The RSA endpoint is an Ekerå–Håstad-style model with explicit accepted-key and success assumptions; its logical resource ceilings use exact arbitrary one-qubit semantics and supply neither a Clifford+T approximation certificate nor physical surface-code runtimes. The P-256 construction concerns elliptic-curve discrete logarithms rather than integer factoring.

This study generator has separate caps: six integer bits, twelve phase bits, forty declared qubits, 250,000 actual lowered operations per trial, 64 complete retries, five cases and eight native queries per sweep. Each native query runs in an isolated process with at most 90 seconds of wall time. Generation/retry guards, native-query limits and unavailable or timed-out native jobs can leave a workload without a computed physical report. Diagnostic simulation/check caps are separate: those checks can be recorded as

or partial coverage even when a conditional resource estimate of the materialized circuit is available. Detached code downloads can omit historical baseline files; their absence is labeled separately from verified preservation in a source checkout.

The study records exact parameters, package versions, source revision/content hashes, diagnostic coverage, whole-workload budgets and limits. Its per-method QASM and resource reports are linked through the manifest. The N15/t4 default and frozen Grover baseline retain their original meanings.
